entry.title: Decorrelation Stretch Technique Reveals Faded Ancient Images
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | spinoff.nasa.gov | hacker news

Decorrelation stretch, an image processing technique developed at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory for satellite imagery, is being used to reveal faded ancient rock art and archaeological features. The method works by mapping colors to an expanded range, which increases contrast and makes subtle visual details visible in imagery that is otherwise difficult to see.

The Dstretch plug-in and mobile apps, developed by researcher Jon Harman, have helped uncover previously undocumented paintings in Cambodia, Norway, and Egypt. Beyond rock art, the technology is used for tracking volcanic plumes, identifying buried structures via aerial imagery, and enhancing tattoos on mummified remains.

entry.title: The Psychological Impact of Software Development Processes
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | graybeard.ing | hacker news

The unique characteristics of software development—including high velocity, low physical friction for changes, and complex abstractions—often cause developers and managers to lose a sense of proportion. Because digital changes lack the visible costs of physical construction, they frequently accumulate hidden architectural and cognitive debt, triggering an unhealthy sense of urgency and a cycle of unnecessary iteration.

Complexity often serves to provide psychological rewards and social status, imbuing mundane tasks with a false sense of importance. An industry-wide obsession with velocity and continuous "pivoting" discourages the practice of leaving stable systems alone, ultimately leading to a state of permanent, unnecessary mutation.

While the engine has achieved significant technical milestones, the shift toward a more permissive LLM policy has resulted in a loss of trust in governance and a perceived influx of low-effort, AI-generated content in community sharing channels.

The author argues that disruptive behavior and the inability to moderate "dunking" have caused a "ratchet effect," where the exodus of original community members leaves behind a space dominated by increasingly caustic norms.

entry.title: Google DeepMind Launches AlphaGenome Atlas
entry.content:
Techmeme | blog.google | hacker news

AlphaGenome Atlas is a 1-petabyte database that predicts the regulatory impact of every possible single nucleotide variant in the human genome. Using the AlphaGenome AI model, the platform maps 9 billion single-letter genetic changes across both coding and non-coding DNA regions to help clarify the functional significance of the genome.

The platform introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score, a single metric designed to help researchers quickly prioritize impactful variants for study. Researchers have already used the tool to identify a critical variant in the DNM1 gene for rare disease research and to uncover genetic regions linked to body mass index (BMI). The Atlas is accessible through a web portal requiring no coding skills.

entry.content:

These configurations are often kept in private repositories to mitigate security risks, such as network mapping, and to protect personal contact information. Beyond security, the files serve as an intimate "render of the brain," encoding highly individualistic idiosyncrasies, social connections, and personal histories.

entry.title: Insilico's Rentosertib Shows Potential for Biological Age Reversal
entry.content:
Techmeme | nytimes.com | source

Insilico reports that early data from Phase 2a clinical trials of rentosertib, an AI-designed drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), suggests the treatment may slow biological aging. Analysis of blood samples from 42 patients across six independent proteomic aging clocks indicated a consistent reduction in predicted biological age among treated individuals.

The findings, published in Nature Biotechnology, demonstrate the potential for using proteomic biomarkers to track geroscience-related outcomes during drug development. Rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor, has progressed to Phase III clinical trials to further evaluate its efficacy and impact on lung function.

entry.title: The Decline of Literacy in a Digital Age
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | edwest.co.uk | hacker news

The shift from deep reading to mindless digital consumption through smartphones and social media is eroding cognitive attention and cultural complexity. This trend, examined in relation to James Marriott's book *The New Dark Ages*, suggests the emergence of a post-literate society characterized by increasingly fragmented attention spans.

Simplification is becoming evident in pop music, scientific research, and political discourse. As attention spans decrease, the capacity for deep, focused concentration is being replaced by rapid, superficial stimulation, which may fundamentally alter democratic engagement and human empathy.

entry.title: Fifth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of Jackson Water Contamination Lawsuit
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | motherjones.com | source | hacker news

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of a lawsuit brought by Jackson, Mississippi residents alleging that the city's failure to prevent lead-contaminated water exposure violated their constitutional rights. Judge Kurt Engelhardt ruled that the U.S. Constitution does not grant a right to truthful information from officials or a right to clean water during a public health crisis.

The ruling follows years of infrastructure neglect in the majority-Black, high-poverty city, where lead levels have been a concern since at least 2015. While several U.S. states and various international governments have enshrined the right to clean water in their constitutions, the federal ruling limits the scope of such constitutional claims. The decision coincides with recent EPA proposals to weaken Clean Water Act protections.
